Remark
[energy minima need not be minimal geodesics]

Source: petersen:page-0203 ↗ thm:pet-ch5-energy-minima-geodesics Local minima of $E$ characterize geodesics, but not every geodesic is a local minimum. In $\mathbb R^n$ all geodesics are integral curves of globally defined distance functions $u(x)=v\cdot x$; on the unit sphere, however, no geodesic of length $>\pi $ is locally minimizing, since it forms part of a great circle whose complementary arc has length $<\pi $, giving a shorter competitor.
